transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes, absolutely. That funny smell is probably lint or fluff getting scorched on the heating element because it can't escape properly due to a blockage. This also explains why it isn't drying: if air can't flow through the clothes, moisture stays trapped. The most common fix is to clean the lint filter (usually behind a small door at the bottom front) and, if your model has one, the condenser unit inside that same compartment. Please do this with the machine unplugged. If you find it full of fluff or debris, clean it thoroughly and try a smaller load on a drying cycle to see if the smell disappears.
Ok, I'll have a look. It's a hot burning dust sort of smell, and the top of the machine feels very hot to touch while drying. I've still been using it though. Should I be worried?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, you should be concerned. A 'hot burning dust' smell combined with the top getting very hot suggests lint or fluff is being drawn onto a hot surface because airflow is restricted; this is a fire risk and means the dryer is overheating. Please stop using it until you have checked for blockages. Please check three things: 1) Is the main lint filter in the door opening clear of all fluff? 2) If your model has a condenser unit (a plastic grid behind a small flap at the bottom front), is that clean and dry inside? These checks are safe to do now.

Ok, I'll stop using it and unplug it. I'm not sure whether mine has a condenser, I didn't know it needed cleaning. Do I just check the filter and then try it again, or should I get someone out to look at it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The burning smell and heat suggest fluff is getting trapped near hot parts because airflow is restricted. Please unplug it and check the main lint filter in the door opening, and if your model has one (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front), remove and rinse the condenser unit under cold water to clear any fluff. Let both dry completely before putting them back. If they were clogged, this is likely the cause; if they are already clean, the blockage may be deeper in the vent hose or internal ducting, which requires an engineer to check safely.
Ok, it's unplugged now. So if the filter looks clean, I should get an engineer out? Or is it fine to try it again once I've cleaned things?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If the filters are clear but it still smells of burning dust and gets very hot, do not try to run it again yet. The heat suggests a deeper blockage in the internal ducting or a failing fan, which requires an engineer to check safely. Please unplug it and check the lint filter in the door opening, and if your model has one (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front), remove and rinse the condenser unit under cold water to clear any fluff. Let both dry completely before putting them back.
